questions.instructions: `hook` is the one-line summary of a stored memory note and `body` is the full note. Does the note claim that a tool, command, library or feature is broken, lacks a capability or cannot do something - a claim that would make a reader avoid it or work around it - without naming a version or a date the claim was observed on? A note that explains how a tool behaves and what to do about it (a usage trap together with the working way, a rule for using it correctly) is NOT such a claim, even when it says that a wrong usage fails.

criteria.true: it claims a tool is broken or cannot do something, so a reader would avoid it, and names no version or date
criteria.false: it makes no such claim, it describes a usage trap together with the working way, or the claim names a version or a date

questions.instructions: `hook` is the one-line summary of a stored memory note and `body` is the full note. Is the note's lesson tied to one specific past version of a tool or library - a bug fixed in a named release, an upgrade or migration that has been completed, a result measured on one named version - rather than to how the tool behaves in general?

criteria.true: its lesson stands or falls with one named past version, release, upgrade or migration
criteria.false: its lesson is about general behaviour, or a version it names is only an example
